questions.question: In which year was the term 'secular' added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **term 'secular' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.**
 
• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution originally did not contain the term 'secular'. It was added later to reflect the secular nature of the Indian state.
 
• The **42ⁿd Amendment Act, of 1976, was passed during the period of Emergency in India,** and it brought about many significant changes to the Constitution.
 
• 
 
The ‘Preamble’ of the Constitution of India is a brief introductory statement that sets out the guiding purpose and principles of the document, and it indicates the source from which the document which derives its authority, meaning, the people.

 
 
• It was adopted on 26 November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly of India and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• After the 42nd amendment, three new terms "Socialist, Secular, and Integrity" were added to the Preamble.
 
 
• 42ⁿd Amendment Act, 1976 is one of the most important amendments to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was enacted by the Indian National Congress headed by Indira Gandhi.
 
• Due to the large number of amendments this act has brought to the Indian Constitution, it is also known as the ‘Mini-Constitution.’ 
 
 
 
• Only one time the Preamble was amended in 1976 till date.
 
• 
 
Thus, it is clear that through the 42nd Amendment the word 'secular' is added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 
• 
 
41st Amendment Act- Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission's retirement age changed from 60 to 62 years(article 316).

 
 
• 43rd Amendment Act- 
 
 
• Deprived parliament to make law for anti-nationalists.
 
• Restoring judicial reviews and writs of SC and HC.
 
 
 
• 44th Amendment Act- Right to property, not a fundamental right. It has been shifted from Article 31 to 300A.

questions.question: ________ provides supporting services in the main areas of industrial and agricultural production, domestic and foreign trade, and commerce.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Infrastructure.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infrastructure refers to the basic physical and organizational structures needed for the operation of a society or enterprise, including transportation, communication, and distribution networks.**
 
• Supporting services in** industrial and agricultural production require infrastructure such as roads, rail networks, ports, and airports to transport goods and raw materials.**
 
• **Domestic and foreign trade** and commerce require infrastructure such as telecommunications networks, internet connectivity, and financial institutions to facilitate transactions.
 
• Education and communication are also important for economic development, but they are not directly related to providing support services in the main areas of production and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Education:** Education is important for human capital development and innovation, which can contribute to economic growth. However, it is not a direct supporting service in the main areas of production and trade.
 
• **Communication: **Communication is essential for the exchange of information and ideas, but it is not a physical infrastructure required for production and trade.
 
• **Trade: **Trade refers to the exchange of goods and services between countries or regions, and it requires infrastructure such as transportation and communication networks to facilitate transactions.
 
• **Infrastructure:** Infrastructure includes physical structures such as roads, bridges, ports, and airports, as well as organizational structures such as financial institutions and regulatory frameworks. It is essential for economic development and growth.

- Option 2, "Tenant Society", refers to an organization representing the interests of tenants, who are people who rent land from landlords. This option is incorrect as the Landholders Society represented the interests of landlords, not tenants.

questions.question: A reaction in which reactants combine to form products and again products recombine to form reactants is called _____ reaction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** reversible.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A reversible reaction is a chemical reaction in which the products can react to form the original reactants.**
 
• Such reactions occur in** both directions and reach a state of equilibrium where the forward and reverse reactions are balanced.**
 
• An example of a reversible reaction is the formation of hydrogen iodide from hydrogen and iodine, and its decomposition back into hydrogen and iodine.
 
• Irreversible reactions, on the other hand, proceed only in one direction and cannot be reversed without the addition of another chemical reaction.
 
• Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons from one reactant to another, resulting in a change in oxidation states. They can be reversible or irreversible depending on the reaction conditions.
 
• Displacement reactions involve the replacement of an ion in a compound by another ion. For example, the reaction between copper sulfate and iron produces iron sulfate and copper.

questions.question: Which House of the States participates (s) in the election of the President of India?

options.text: Neither Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
Both, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Legislative Assembly.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Legislative Assembly participates in the election of the President of India.**
 
• The President is elected through an** electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.**
 
• The Legislative Council does not participate in the** election of the President.**
 
• The primary function of the Legislative Council is to act as a check on the Legislative Assembly and not to participate in the election of the President.
 
• The election of the President of India is an indirect election, where the people do not directly elect the President but instead elect representatives who then elect the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both the Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and the Union Territories of Delhi and Pondicherry.
 
• Article 52 of the Constitution of India deals with the office of President.
 
• The manner of election of the President is provided by Article 55 of the Constitution.
 
• The general principle of the election of the President is that the total number of votes cast by a Member of Parliament equals the total number of votes cast by state legislators.
 
• Part 5 of the Constitution under Chapter 1 (The Executive) lists out the qualification, election, and impeachment of the President of India **(Article 52-Article 62).**

questions.question: Buddha belonged to a smaller order called Shakya Gana, and was a _______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Siddhartha Gautama, who later became known as the Buddha or "The Enlightened One", was born into the Shakya clan.
 
• This was a community located in the foothills of the Himalayas in modern-day Nepal
 
• The community was organized as a republic or 'gana', often translated as a tribal federation or oligarchy.
 
• Buddha's father, Suddhodana, was an elected leader or chief of this 'gana'.
 
• The Shakyas were a part of the Kshatriya varna, or warrior/ruler class in the traditional Hindu social hierarchy. Hence, Buddha was a Kshatriya by birth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kshatriyas were the second-highest class in the Varna system and were responsible for protecting the society and maintaining law and order.
 
• Vaishyas were the third-highest class and were involved in trade, agriculture, and commerce.
 
• Shudras were the lowest class and were considered to be socially inferior to the other three classes.
 
• The Varna system was a rigid social structure, and people were not allowed to move up or down the social ladder based on their abilities or achievements. It was abolished in independent India, but its remnants still exist in some parts of the country.

questions.question: In _______, a crisis in the balance of payments led to the introduction of economic reforms in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1991.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The economic crisis in the balance of payments was triggered by a sharp increase in oil prices, which led to a surge in imports and a depletion of foreign exchange reserves.**
 
• The government of India was forced to seek a bailout loan from the** International Monetary Fund (IMF) to avoid defaulting on its external debt payments.**
 
• As a condition for the loan, the IMF demanded a set of economic reforms that aimed to address the structural weaknesses of the Indian economy, including its high fiscal deficit, inflation, and inefficient public sector enterprises.
 
• The reforms, known as the** New Economic Policy (NEP) or the Liberalization-Privatization-Globalization (LPG) policy,** included measures such as reducing trade barriers, deregulating industries, attracting foreign investment, and cutting subsidies.
 
• The NEP was controversial and faced opposition from various quarters, including political parties, trade unions, and farmers, who argued that it favored big businesses and foreign interests at the expense of domestic industries and workers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1997 was not a significant year** in India's economic history. It was a year of relative stability and growth, with the economy expanding at a rate of around 7%.
 
• **2001 was a year of global economic slowdown and uncertainty,** following the dot-com bubble burst and the 9/11 attacks. India's economy was affected by these events, but it did not experience a crisis in the balance of payments.
 
• **1981 was a year of economic difficulties for India, **marked by high inflation, low growth, and a fiscal deficit. However, it was not a year of balance of payments crisis, as India had a surplus in its current account and foreign exchange reserves.
